channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Election Commission Warns Officials Against Interference
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission has met with local authorities and law enforcement ahead of the January 27, 2027 presidential elections. Officials were warned against interfering in the electoral process, emphasizing transparency and legality. Preparations for polling stations and new technologies were also discussed.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Bank Buys More Gold, Maintaining Strong Reserve Position
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank acquired an additional 5 tons of gold in September, reinforcing its position as a leading gold purchaser. The country ranks fourth globally in gold purchases both for the month and year-to-date. The bank plans to reduce gold's share in reserves from 78% to 75% by year-end.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Supreme Audit Chamber Uncovers Billions in Gas Sector Violations
item.description: Kazakhstan's Supreme Audit Chamber has identified financial irregularities totaling 24.1 billion tenge within the gas industry. Inefficient planning and budget spending amounted to 18.2 billion tenge. While some funds were recovered, the chamber noted that domestic gas production lags behind growing demand, and gas quality is inconsistent.

item.title: Tajikistan's Rogun Dam: Building the World's Tallest Dam for Regional Power
item.description: The Rogun Hydropower Plant in Tajikistan is constructing the world's tallest dam, a project of significant regional importance. With a projected power generation capacity of nearly 17 billion kWh, the dam is seen as a symbol of Tajik resilience and meticulous engineering, attracting global attention.

item.title: Almaty Hosts International Conference on Microbiology and Virology Milestones
item.description: Almaty celebrated the 70th anniversary of the Research Institute of Microbiology and Virology and the 75th birthday of academician Amankeldi Sadanov. The international scientific conference focused on biotechnology development and biosafety, with participation from scientists across Central Asia and beyond.

item.title: Two Officials Punished for Inaction in Turkestan Region's Investment Project
item.description: Two officials in the Turkestan region have been disciplined for inaction that hindered the launch of a 2.8 billion tenge cotton processing plant. The prosecutor's office intervened to resolve infrastructure issues, ensuring the plant reached its design capacity and boosting regional agricultural processing.

item.title: Kazakhstan Police Seize 10 Kilograms of Synthetic Drugs in Aktobe
item.description: Transport police in Aktobe, Kazakhstan, have seized 10 kilograms of the synthetic drug alpha-PVP. A pre-trial investigation has been launched into the distribution channel. Suspects, who allegedly operated as 'warehouse workers' for a drug store, rented a house for packaging. Police found drugs in the house and a nearby forest. The suspects face up to 15 years in prison.

item.title: Audit of Kazakhstan's Gas Sector Reveals Violations Worth 24.1 Billion Tenge
item.description: An audit of Kazakhstan's gas sector has uncovered financial violations totaling 24.1 billion tenge, according to the Supreme Audit Chamber. The audit also highlighted issues with supplying the domestic market with commercial gas and the wear of gas transportation infrastructure. Gas reserves in Kazakhstan are estimated at 3.8 trillion cubic meters.

item.title: Industrial Production in Almaty's Zhetysu District Grows by 8.5%
item.description: Industrial production in the Zhetysu district of Almaty has increased by 8.5%. Construction and entrepreneurship also show positive dynamics. The district is developing new industrial sites and expanding existing enterprises. Small and medium-sized businesses are thriving, with tax revenues increasing by 11% and nearly 4,000 jobs created.

item.title: Almaty's Zhetysu District Opens 1,520 New School Places, Expands Extracurricular Education
item.description: Almaty's Zhetysu district has opened 1,520 new school places through new construction and reconstruction. A new school building for School No. 112 and an additional building for School No. 43 are also under construction. The district plans to establish an Innovation Center for Creativity and expand library and sports facilities.

item.title: Astana Gridlocked by 10-Point Traffic Jams Due to Foreign Leader Visits
item.description: Astana experienced severe traffic congestion, with road load reaching 10 points, due to visits by foreign delegations. King Abdullah II of Jordan, President Emomali Rahmon of Tajikistan, and a summit for the Aqaba Process are in the capital. Residents expressed frustration over prolonged road closures impacting daily commutes and emergency services.

item.title: State Audit Uncovers Billions in Financial Violations in Kazakhstan's Gas Sector
item.description: A state audit in Kazakhstan has revealed billions of tenge in financial irregularities within the country's gas industry. The findings highlight significant mismanagement and potential corruption within the sector, prompting calls for reform and accountability.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Red Book Unrevised for Nearly 20 Years, Experts Warn
item.description: The Red Book of Kyrgyzstan has not been updated in nearly two decades, despite a required 10-year revision cycle. The last edition was published in 2007. Preparation for the third edition is underway, but budget cuts threaten its timely release, with specialists estimating a need for $500,000.

item.title: Kazakhstan Doctors Preserve Fertility in Women Treated for Endometrial Cancer
item.description: Doctors at the Kazakh Research Institute of Oncology and Radiology have successfully preserved fertility in women diagnosed with endometrial cancer. Through hormonal therapy, three patients have overcome cancer and given birth to healthy children, demonstrating that treatment is possible even with malignant tumors.

item.title: Pakistan's Military Seeks Geopolitical Advantage Amid Regional Instability
item.description: Pakistan's military leadership is leveraging regional instability to enhance its geopolitical standing. Recent visits to Tehran highlight Islamabad's strategy of positioning itself as an indispensable stakeholder benefiting from crises, rather than just a participant. This opportunistic diplomacy aims to maximize strategic relevance across various regional actors.

item.title: Almaty Implements New Differentiated Parking Fees Starting October 4
item.description: Almaty has introduced new differentiated parking fees, ranging from 100 to 200 tenge per hour, depending on location and demand. The city aims to increase parking space turnover and ease parking searches. The new system, approved by the maslikhat, took effect on October 4, replacing the previous flat rate of 100 tenge.

item.title: New System to Aid Rescues in Almaty Mountains Undergoing Testing
item.description: A new safety system is being tested in Almaty to help rescuers locate individuals in mountainous areas, even without mobile or internet access. The AG Tag device uses satellite navigation to transmit coordinates to rescue services, updating every two seconds. An SOS button allows tourists to send an emergency signal.

item.title: Tajikistan Ministry of Internal Affairs Reports Arrest of Nine Suspected Drug Smugglers
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Internal Affairs announced the detention of nine individuals suspected of drug trafficking. The group allegedly smuggled over half a ton of narcotics from Afghanistan into Tajikistan for international distribution over the past year. Authorities seized 24 kilograms of hashish in the Matchin district, with the intended destination undisclosed.

item.title: Bishkek and Chuy Region Enforce Ban on Fine-Coal Imports
item.description: A ban on the import, sale, storage, and use of fine-fraction coal (0-13 mm) remains in effect in Bishkek and the Chuy Region. The city hall reminds residents of restrictions and offers preferential loans for transitioning to cleaner heating systems. Exceptions are made for heat-supplying enterprises.

item.title: Large Synthetic Drug Trafficking Channel Disrupted in Aktobe
item.description: Transport police in Aktobe have stopped a criminal group involved in distributing synthetic drugs. During a special operation, 10 kg of Alpha-PVP psychotropic substance were seized, disrupting a major drug trafficking channel. The suspects acted as a drug warehouse, fulfilling orders from an anonymous operator.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee Mandates Traffic Routing Through State Node
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) has ordered hosting providers and mobile operators to route internet traffic through the state's main telecommunications hub. This directive aims to enhance control over internet infrastructure and data flow within the country.

item.title: Kazakh Enterprise Head Sentenced to Six Years for Fraud
item.description: The head of a company in Kazakhstan's Kostanay region has been sentenced to six years in prison for fraud. He was found guilty of selling 352.56 tons of wheat belonging to another farm and failing to pay transport services totaling 11.1 million tenge.

item.title: Kazakhstan National Bank to Sell $910 Million, Explore Digital Tenge
item.description: The National Bank of Kazakhstan plans to gradually sell $910 million on the foreign exchange market, according to its head, Timur Suleimenov. He stated that the sales will not impact the fundamental functioning of the currency market and are not linked to new transfers from the National Fund. Suleimenov also addressed increased currency trading volumes, attributing them to fundamental factors like a strong balance of payments and export surplus.

item.title: Russian Businessman and Higgsfield Co-founder Alex Mashrabov Granted Kazakh Citizenship
item.description: Alex Mashrabov, a Russian businessman and co-founder of the AI media content platform Higgsfield, has been granted citizenship of Kazakhstan. The company stated that Higgsfield has strong ties to Kazakhstan, indicating the significance of this development for the tech sector in the country.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Increase Threshold for Monitoring Mobile Money Transfers
item.description: Starting November 10, Kazakhstan will raise the threshold for monitoring mobile money transfers to 537,000 tenge per quarter. While the total amount for three months will increase to 1.557 million tenge, this change does not permit accepting payments for goods and services via personal cards. Banks will report suspicious transactions to tax authorities.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Debates Ban on Energy Drinks Amid Health Concerns
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a complete ban on the production and import of energy drinks, as proposed by President Sadyr Japarov. This initiative stems from concerns over public health impacts, with consumption figures showing millions of liters consumed annually. While a ban could cost the budget billions of soms, the president emphasizes national health over financial gains. An alternative proposal suggests restricting sales to minors and increasing risk awareness.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Insurance for Foreign Trucks on State Borders
item.description: Kazakhstan is discussing reforms to its road toll system for trucks, aiming for self-sustaining road infrastructure. A working group, chaired by the Deputy Prime Minister, reviewed proposals to improve existing toll collection and funding for road maintenance. Suggestions include aligning toll rates with regional levels and potentially requiring insurance for foreign trucks crossing the border.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Interior Ministry to Oversee Gas and Coal Supply to Households
item.description: Uzbekistan's Interior Ministry held a meeting to ensure stable gas and coal supply to households and social facilities, and to prevent corruption. In October, 16 cases of illegal coal storage and sale were identified, with 333.54 tons confiscated. Additionally, 374 cases involving liquefied gas were found, leading to the confiscation of 9,139 gas cylinders and 92.9 tons of gas.

item.title: New York Court Temporarily Blocks Deportation of Over 150 Afghans
item.description: A federal judge in New York has temporarily halted the deportation of over 150 Afghan citizens. These individuals include those who collaborated with U.S. forces in Afghanistan and their relatives. Critics fear persecution upon return.

item.title: 90 Million Displaced People Face Climate Threats, UN Refugee Agency Warns
item.description: The UN refugee agency reports that nearly 90 million forcibly displaced people are living in countries highly exposed to climate hazards like droughts and floods. Over two-thirds of refugee returns in early 2026 were to such at-risk areas, potentially leading to renewed displacement. The agency calls for increased funding for climate adaptation in vulnerable communities.

item.title: Tashkent: Two Suspected of Kidnapping for Hire Apprehended
item.description: Two individuals in Tashkent have been apprehended on suspicion of kidnapping for hire. A citizen reported being forcibly taken into a vehicle but managed to escape. Investigations revealed Telegram communications with a client detailing the plan to abduct the victim. The suspects, previously convicted for theft, were found with an axe.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Congratulates Nation on Constitution's 32nd Anniversary
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon congratulated the nation on the 32nd anniversary of the Constitution's adoption. He described the Constitution's adoption during the civil war as a historic achievement and a result of the Tajik people's efforts for independence. Rahmon emphasized respecting and adhering to constitutional values.

item.title: Bishkek Sends Note to Moscow Requesting Return of Kyrgyz Citizen from Russian Military Unit
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's embassy in Moscow has sent a note to the Russian Foreign Ministry urging the return of a Kyrgyz citizen, 21-year-old Elistan Toktogulov. Relatives claim he was deceived into coming to Russia for work and then sent to a military unit, possibly for deployment to Ukraine. Bishkek seeks a thorough investigation.

item.title: Afghanistan Has Potential to Generate 220 GW of Solar Power, UNDP Reports
item.description: Afghanistan possesses the potential to generate up to 220 gigawatts of solar energy, yet it spends over $280 million annually on electricity imports, according to the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). Tapping into this potential could reduce reliance on foreign supplies and expand access to clean energy.

item.title: Ankara Believes Russia Does Not Meet Requirements for Observer Status in Turkic States
item.description: Ankara believes Russia does not meet the requirements for observer status in the Organization of Turkic States (OTS), according to Kursad Zorlu, deputy chairman of Turkey's ruling Justice and Development Party. This statement follows a proposal by Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev to grant Russia observer status or include it in the 'OTS Plus' format.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Updates Rules for Monopoly Control and Company Mergers
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has revised its regulations for antitrust control, including rules for company mergers, joint ventures, and state aid to businesses. The Antimonopoly Service will now review company actions that could affect market competition, such as mergers and acquisitions. New provisions also empower the service to assess the competitive impact of state financial assistance to enterprises.

item.title: New Mayor Appointed in Kara-Balta Amid Environmental Scandal
item.description: Asylbek Jenishbek has been appointed the new mayor of Kara-Balta, a city facing ongoing complaints about industrial air pollution. The appointment by President Sadyr Japarov comes amid heightened environmental concerns, with residents reporting smog and industrial emissions. Authorities have taken measures against polluting enterprises, including "Asia Steel," which was identified as a major source of emissions.

item.title: Uralsk: Life in Kazakhstan's 'Western Gateway' City Bordering Russia
item.description: Uralsk, Kazakhstan's western gateway, is closer to Russian cities like Samara than to its own regional centers. This report explores how proximity to Russia impacts the lives of residents in Uralsk and five other border cities, as part of a special project on the Kazakh-Russian border.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Enhance Sales Control with Fiscal Software Mandate
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has approved regulations for fiscal software with data transmission capabilities, signed by Cabinet of Ministers Chairman Adylbek Kasymaliev. This aims to improve tax administration and ensure accurate revenue accounting. Certain business activities will require mandatory use of this software, with others able to use it voluntarily.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Increase Outsourcing in State Healthcare to 30% by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to expand private sector involvement in its healthcare system, aiming to procure 30% of medical services through outsourcing by 2030. The initiative, outlined in a presidential decree, also involves attracting foreign professional management companies to at least five major medical institutions to implement advanced management practices. Mechanisms for private sector engagement, considering regional healthcare needs and existing capacities, will be introduced from January 1, 2027.
